source.notes: No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. From the CISCE Archive Library ISC 2018 question-paper bundle (a Word-generated PDF with a real text layer). Paper code '1218-860' printed in the footer of every page. Cover: '(Maximum Marks: 100)', '(Time allowed: Three hours)', additional 15 minutes reading time, 6 printed pages. Section A (80 marks) is compulsory; candidates attempt all questions EITHER from Section B (vectors, 3-D geometry, area; 20 marks) OR Section C (commerce/economics applications, regression, linear programming; 20 marks). Both Sections B and C are included, so the pack's marks total (120 counting one alternative per OR pair) exceeds maxMarks (100) by design. Question 1 is printed '[10×2]' and Questions 15 and 19 '[3×2]'; each sub-part is its own entry. OR choices (Q5, 8, 9, 10, 13, 16, 17, 20, 21) share a choiceGroup equal to the question number; alternatives labelled (a)/(b) as printed. Notation: the paper uses Cambria Math equation objects; stacked fractions, determinants, matrices, piecewise functions, radicals, integral limits, inverse-trig indices and unit-vector hats are lost or scrambled in the text layer and were rebuilt inline from pypdfium2 page renders (flagged, confidence MEDIUM). Math-italic letters (e.g. '𝑥') are normalised to plain letters. Printed oddities kept as printed: 'semi-verticle' (Q8(b)); the third term '(b⃗×a⃗)' in Q16(a) (confirmed from the glyph codes in the text layer). Q1(i) (binary operation) is mapped to relations-and-functions. Regression items (Q19(b), Q20) have no matching chapter slug and are left with chapter null. No cognitive-level tags are printed on this paper.
source.usage: Official CISCE board examination paper from the CISCE Archive Library (cisce.org/archive-library); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text: A manufacturing company makes two types of teaching aids A and B of Mathematics for Class X. Each type of A requires 9 labour hours for fabricating and 1 labour hour for finishing. Each type of B requires 12 labour hours for fabricating and 3 labour hours for finishing. For fabricating and finishing, the maximum labour hours available per week are 180 and 30 respectively. The company makes a profit of ₹ 80 on each piece of type A and ₹ 120 on each piece of type B. How many pieces of type A and type B should be manufactured per week to get a maximum profit? Formulate this as Linear Programming Problem and solve it. Identify the feasible region from the rough sketch.
